title: Discriminative vs. Generative Models
description: Two opposite ways of learning from data - drawing a decision boundary between classes versus modeling how the data itself is generated - and which algorithms belong to each camp.
content:
Machine learning models can be split into two families depending on what they learn: **discriminative** and **generative** models.

**Discriminative models** focus on learning a decision boundary between different classes or categories. They learn the conditional probability of the output given the input, i.e. they directly map an input X to an output Y.

Examples of discriminative models:
• Linear Regression
• Logistic Regression
• Support Vector Machines
• Multilayer Perceptron

**Generative models** learn the underlying data distribution and generate new samples from it. They attempt to model the joint distribution of input and output simultaneously by trying to capture how the data is generated, including the underlying structure of the inputs themselves.

Examples of generative models:
• Naive Bayes
• Gaussian Mixture Models
• Generative Adversarial Networks
• Variational Autoencoders

In short: discriminative models learn P(Y|X) - how to tell the classes apart - while generative models learn P(X, Y) - how the data could have been produced, which also lets them create new, similar samples.
